Four panes, one source, two compilers. The first and third compile the by-value form
(the buffer element is passed as a function argument); the second and fourth compile
the direct-indexing form. Everything else is identical.

What to compare: in each pane, where the float-typed structured-buffer load sits
relative to the first conditional branch. In the by-value panes both loads are in the
entry block above a single branch, and the two [branch] conditions have been folded
into one. In the direct-indexing panes the integer load comes first, then a branch,
and the float load is inside the guarded block, so it runs only when the first
condition holds. That one load is the reported cost. Both forms are correct code; the
difference is where the memory access ends up. The last two panes are the in-progress
Clang HLSL compiler on the same input.

This source is a restating of the shader in the issue body: the pixel stage becomes
[numthreads] and discard becomes a store to an RWBuffer, because clang-dxc rejects
discard today and a pane full of that error would say nothing about this issue. The
original pixel spelling was measured locally instead, on a Debug build of main and on
20 stable releases back to v1.4.1907, and this restating was checked to still show
the same difference before it was published here.

Compiler Explorer builds these with debug flags appended, which changes value names
and adds metadata but not the placement being compared.
